findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential never removed
findings.body: After a successful recovery-code login the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) when allCodesUsed(). removeStoredCredentialById only removes a locally stored (Keycloak DB) credential. When the credential was created in user storage via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, the ID is a federated/user-storage ID, so the call does nothing to the external storage (or can target the wrong local row). The consequence is that an exhausted recovery-codes credential stored in user storage is never deleted/disabled and the user is not forced to re-register correctly on subsequent logins.

findings.title: Federated recovery codes never marked as used, allowing replay
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential stores the raw code list in user storage and validation delegates to UserStorageProvider.isValid via user.credentialManager().isValid(). The local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider normally hashes, verifies, and marks the used code as consumed and persists the updated credential. For a federated credential that consumption path is bypassed: the authenticator only reads the credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential and never writes back an updated used-code state to user storage. The bundled test storage BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid only does anyMatch on the stored list and never removes the used code. The consequence is recovery codes backed by user storage remain valid indefinitely and can be replayed, breaking the one-time-use security property.

findings.title: getCredentials dereferences possibly-null user
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials the code does var myUser = getMyUser(user) and then immediately accesses myUser.recoveryCodes and myUser.otp without a null check. Other methods in the same class (isConfiguredFor, isValid, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) explicitly handle myUser == null. If the user is unknown to this storage (different federation, deleted, or lookup by ID miss), getCredentials throws NullPointerException, which can break credential listing, login rendering, and account APIs for unrelated users.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get on recovery credential
findings.body: The constructor does RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) and then immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get() without checking isPresent, and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If the user has no recovery credential in either federated or local storage (race, deleted credential, misconfigured flow rendering the template), this throws NoSuchElementException and produces a 500 instead of a controlled error/fallback. The previous code had the same pattern for local-only storage, but the change extends it to a new federated lookup path without adding the missing empty check.
